prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 2005 manifesto (policy measures only)

Economy and tax
- Add higher income tax bands (e.g., 50% over £50k, 60% over £100k as indicative), add bands to Corporation Tax with 40% for profits over £1.5m.
- Tax unearned income more; replace Inheritance Tax with a progressive levy on recipients.
- Abolish National Insurance and raise equivalent revenue from income (earned and unearned).
- Pilot Land Value Tax set locally to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates.
- Phase out VAT and replace it with revenue‑neutral eco‑taxes tied to resource use, pollution and waste.
- Promote economic localisation via community banks, credit unions, micro‑credit, and potential local currencies; oppose joining the euro.
- Support workers’ rights, unionisation, and reduced working hours; back a Charter of Workers’ Rights.
- Replace GDP with broader wellbeing metrics (e.g., ISEW/MDP).

Energy and climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence; reduce UK CO2 20% by 2010, 50% by 2020, 85% by 2030.
- Replace domestic VAT and the Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax based on fuel carbon content; abolish standing charges and use rising block tariffs.
- Target 40% of energy from renewables by 2020; reallocate R&D and subsidies from nuclear to renewables; deploy solar PV and small wind at scale; expand biogas.
- Reduce demand via a Warmer Homes Act (30% cut in domestic energy use in 10 years) and local Smart Energy Councils.
- Decommission nuclear stations at end of life and end nuclear R&D subsidies.

Welfare, housing, work
- Phase in a universal, unconditional Citizen’s Income replacing most means‑tested benefits (with disability/incapacity benefits retained; housing benefit integrated later).
- Introduce a universal Citizen’s Pension linked to average earnings, replacing Pension Credit.
- Simplify child support by folding means‑tested elements into a higher universal child payment; expand Sure Start; end Working Time Directive opt‑out and examine a 35‑hour week.
- Boost social housing: allow councils to reinvest sale receipts; support self‑build co‑ops; improve insulation and efficiency.

Health and education
- Restore a comprehensive, publicly provided NHS; end prescription charges; reinstate free eye tests and NHS dentistry; expand access to complementary treatments.
- Increase health funding to at least 9% of GNP (~£90bn by 2008); consider a hypothecated NHS tax.
- Increase education funding, especially pre‑school and post‑16; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; abolish SATs and introduce voluntary Individual Learning Plans.

Transport
- Target a 10% road traffic reduction by 2010; divert £30bn from road‑building to public transport.
- Return rail and Underground to public ownership; re‑regulate buses; invest in light rail and integrated ticketing.
- Expand congestion charging/road pricing where effective; raise fuel duty and abolish the car tax disc; scale freight duties by size/axle/pollution; fund R&D into efficient vehicles.
- Resist airport expansion; ban night flights; seek an EU aviation fuel tax; introduce a UK emissions tax for domestic flights; raise Air Passenger Duty.

Environment, food, farming, animal welfare
- Implement a national Zero Waste Strategy; ban incineration; set recycled‑content standards; create a Zero Waste Agency; reach 60% domestic recycling by 2010.
- Establish an Environmental Protection Commission; levy eco‑taxes on aggregates, pesticides, organochlorines, fossil fuels; strengthen EU chemicals rules.
- Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation, nanotechnology; oppose patents on natural resources; reform WTO TRIPS accordingly.
- End live animal exports; ban battery eggs (including “enriched” cages); press for stricter EU broiler rules; ban fur imports.
- Pass an Organics Target Bill (30% production by 2012); replace CAP/CFP with support for organics, local markets and biodiversity; ban GM food.
- Toughen and enforce a binding supermarkets’ Code of Practice; review OFT approach to convenience store acquisitions.

Crime and justice
- Invest in prevention: safer urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, more staff in public spaces; treat drug misuse primarily as a health issue.
- Expand community policing, local stations, and neighbourhood committees; strengthen independent complaints systems.
- Tighten gun laws (quantitative lethality threshold; prohibit handguns/multishot/high‑calibre/auto and some semi‑auto; regulate deactivated guns; single licensing with safety and suitability tests).
- Embed restorative justice; enhance strategies against hate crimes and violence against women; support a broad European disability directive.

Democracy and governance
- Oppose national ID cards and a central biometric database.
- Reinforce local government powers and finance (including Land Value Tax); enable local recalls and referenda; introduce PR for local councils and Westminster.
- Create elected regional bodies where supported; extend Scottish/Welsh powers if desired.
- Replace the House of Lords with a fully elected chamber by PR; establish a Constitutional Commission for a written constitution; disestablish the Church of England; remove monarchic legislative/executive/judicial roles.
- Oppose the proposed EU constitution while seeking EU reforms that strengthen the Parliament.

International, aid, trade, migration
- Seek withdrawal of UK forces from Iraq in favour of UN peacekeepers; reduce defence spending to the EU average; decommission nuclear weapons; end support for arms exports; pursue an Arms Trade Treaty.
- Raise aid to at least 1% of GNI by 2010; cancel debts of the 52 poorest countries; explore Tobin tax revenues and North–South carbon trading flows.
- Reform the UN Security Council (no permanent seats; majority voting); democratise IMF/World Bank mandates around poverty reduction and sustainability.
- Overhaul WTO rules to enable a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade, allowing preferences for local, rights‑respecting and environmentally responsible trade.
- Improve asylum processing resources, allow work and benefits for asylum seekers, ensure independent appeals, ratify UN conventions on migrants and refugees, and review the Nationality, Immigration and Asylum Act.
